solutions.check: 31 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Leak takes a long time after second tablet

indicators.note: places the long time behind the second and the tablet

blocks.note: an age is a long time

explanation.surface: A slow leak that only starts after someone takes a second pill.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads the long time first, but "after" sends AGE to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: liquid that escapes its container has leaked or spilled, and the noun covers both.

clue.text: Detection devices soundly fixed to joint, by which bits are cut out

definitions.text: by which bits are cut out
definitions.note: a phrase describing the process rather than a plain noun

indicators.note: tells you to go by the sound of the devices, not their spelling
attaches the joint after the first part

blocks.note: sensors detect things; CENSORS is said the same way

explanation.surface: A gadget of sensors bolted onto a joint, sounding like some surgical cutting tool.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a descriptive phrase: censorship is the process by which bits of a text or film are cut out.
explanation.definitionFit: Censorship removes offending parts of a work, so it is what bits are cut out by.

clue.text: Mouthy abuse from upset Labour minister cut short

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the letters bottom to top
tells you to use the shortened form of minister

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for the Labour party
a minister is a reverend, shortened to REV

explanation.surface: A Labour minister, knocked off balance and sacked early, lets rip with a stream of abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: "Labour minister" reads as one politician, but it is two pieces: the party and a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, "verbal" (or "verbals") is a torrent of spoken abuse.

clue.text: (& 7dn.) Pull out hindquarters fluff

blocks.note: the hindquarters are the rear end or rump

explanation.surface: An odd order to tug the fluff out of an animal's rear.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across two grid entries: BACK at 4 down and DOWN at 7 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to retreat from a claim or a fight is to withdraw, the same as pulling out.

clue.text: Second time, right, to have old president hit?

blocks.note: Ike was the nickname of US President Dwight Eisenhower

explanation.surface: Asking whether it's right, a second time round, to have an old president hit.
explanation.walkthrough: Four small pieces in clue order; the only knowledge needed is that IKE is Eisenhower.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym for the verb: to deliver a blow, as in striking a ball or a match.

clue.text: Where many Brits would have Trump stay in September, say party

definitions.text: Where many Brits would have Trump stay in September
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for an adverb of place

blocks.note: a side is a party in a dispute or match

explanation.surface: Many Britons wished Trump would stay home rather than make his state visit in September.
explanation.walkthrough: The long definition is topical: Trump made a state visit to Britain in September 2025, and plenty of Britons would rather he had stayed in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Stateside means in the United States, where these Brits would prefer Trump to remain.

clue.text: Diminished Pence allowed to get in the action

indicators.note: sends the pence and the allowed into the action

blocks.note: a deed is an action; it wraps the rest
P is the abbreviation for pence

explanation.surface: Mike Pence, reduced in stature, is allowed to join in the action.
explanation.walkthrough: Pence looks like the former US vice-president, but here it is only the money, giving P.
explanation.definitionFit: Depleted means diminished or run down.

clue.text: see 4dn.
Old state finally admits boob

indicators.note: takes the last letter of admits

blocks.note: PA is the abbreviation for Pennsylvania, a US state
tit is slang for a breast, a boob

explanation.surface: An old state that at last owns up to its blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: "Boob" looks like a mistake; here it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone past it is too old to do things well.

clue.text: Breaking into house, Dicky turned weak

indicators.note: puts the turned letters inside house
reverses the letters of Dicky

blocks.note: a pad is a house or flat
dicky means ill or unsound; ILL reversed is LLI

explanation.surface: A burglar with a dicky heart feels queasy breaking into a house.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky is British slang for unwell or faulty, as in a dicky heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Pallid means pale and feeble, so weak.

clue.text: The nation emits a lament for all to hear!

indicators.note: says the lament out loud, so go by sound

explanation.surface: A whole country crying out in grief.
explanation.walkthrough: Wales, the nation, is said just like the verb wails.
explanation.definitionFit: Wales is one of the nations of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: What makes Balls tick? Bar!

indicators.note: asks what the letters of BALLS TICK can be made into

explanation.surface: A question about what drives Ed Balls, the former Labour minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Balls reads as Ed Balls, and tick as what motivates him; both words are just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: putting a name on a list of the excluded shuts that person out, as a club bars an unwanted member.

clue.text: Vat blunder in party U-turn

indicators.note: puts the blunder inside the party
reverses the whole result

blocks.note: LAB is short for the Labour party

explanation.surface: A political party blunders into another embarrassing U-turn, this one about vats.
explanation.walkthrough: ERR goes inside LAB to make LERRAB, which reads BARREL backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Near synonym: both are large containers for liquids such as beer or wine.

clue.text: Pissed member brought before bar

indicators.note: puts the member first and the bar after it

blocks.note: a leg is a limb, a member
bar and less both mean except, as in five bar one

explanation.surface: A drunk MP is hauled in front of the bar of the House.
explanation.walkthrough: Bar looks like a pub, which suits the surface, but it means minus. Legless is British slang for very drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Legless is British slang for so drunk you cannot stand.

clue.text: Overcome, try heroin in the sack

indicators.note: puts heroin inside the sack

blocks.note: to have a go is to try
the sack is slang for bed

explanation.surface: Someone urging another to try heroin in bed until overcome.
explanation.walkthrough: The sack is slang for bed, as in hit the sack; the drug sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gobsmacked is British slang for utterly astonished, overcome.

clue.text: After a diet, resist making easy money

indicators.note: 'After' means following, so the resist word follows a diet in the answer

blocks.note: a fast is a diet of nothing
to buck is to resist, as in buck the trend

explanation.surface: Holding out after a crash diet by making a quick profit.
explanation.walkthrough: A fast buck is money made quickly and easily.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: money made quickly with little effort, often slightly shady.

clue.text: (& 17ac./18ac.) Family member – he'd nod off almost, playing with balls

indicators.note: drops the last letter of off
tells you to mix the letters up

blocks.note: HE'D NOD OFF without its last F
taken as written, then mixed with the rest

explanation.surface: A relative dozing off while fiddling with some balls.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer fills three grid entries, 16, 17 and 18 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: your own kin share your body and ancestry, so a relative is described this way.

clue.text: see 16ac.
Americans were hogging the solution

indicators.note: to hog is to keep to yourself, so the words keep the result hidden inside them

explanation.surface: Americans hoarding the fix to some problem.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also the clue's own subject, a solution.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: what solves a problem or puzzle, the very thing a solver writes in the grid.

clue.text: see 16ac.
Judge in too good a light, so stuffed right inside

definitions.text: Judge in too good a light

indicators.note: puts right inside the word for stuffed

blocks.note: if you stuffed yourself, you overate

explanation.surface: Someone praised too highly has been fed a stuffing of flattery.
explanation.walkthrough: OVERATE and OVERRATE differ by one R, which is exactly what the clue adds.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrate is to judge something better than it is.

clue.text: Bars rubbish in deserted suburbs

indicators.note: puts rubbish inside the outer letters
empties suburbs, leaving only its ends

blocks.note: suburbs with its middle emptied out

explanation.surface: Pubs full of rubbish in abandoned outskirts.
explanation.walkthrough: Bars looks like pubs, but it means stripes, as in bands of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: long bands of colour, as on a flag or a sergeant's sleeve.

clue.text: Arse grabbing of French student

indicators.note: the arse word grabs the French and holds it inside

explanation.surface: A French student's bottom being grabbed.
explanation.walkthrough: A reader is someone who reads a subject at university, a student; it is also a lecturer's title in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A reader is someone who studies, a student.

clue.text: Beg US rock band to back pain-in-the-arse

indicators.note: 'back' as a verb means move backwards, as a car backs, so the band's letters run the other way

blocks.note: to bum a cigarette is to beg one
REM, the band from Georgia, backwards

explanation.surface: Pleading with an American band to support you in an annoying situation.
explanation.walkthrough: To back looks like supporting the band, but it means reversing REM.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: an annoying or disappointing situation, informal in both forms.

clue.text: Done by screwing at a distance

indicators.note: twisting the letters, like a screw, rearranges them

explanation.surface: A job done through bolting things together from far away.
explanation.walkthrough: By does double duty: its letters are fodder and it helps signal the twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyond means further away, at a distance.

clue.text: Drink's improved – non-drinker's pissed off

indicators.note: the non-drinker is sent packing, so remove it

blocks.note: TT, teetotal, is a non-drinker; remove it

explanation.surface: A drink got better once the teetotaller cleared off.
explanation.walkthrough: Pissed off looks like annoyed; here it is an order to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the commonest alcoholic drink in a British pub.

clue.text: Awfully shapely bum, but heartless – curses!

definitions.note: plural noun for a singular, uncountable noun

indicators.note: signals the letters are badly arranged
removes the middle letter of bum

explanation.surface: An exclamation on seeing a nicely shaped bottom attached to a cruel person.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram covers SHAPELY plus BM, the shell of bum.
explanation.definitionFit: Oaths that take God's name in vain are profane swearing, the old sense of cursing.

clue.text: Sick of country being forced into exercise

indicators.note: pushes country inside exercise

explanation.surface: A nation tired of being made to do PE.
explanation.walkthrough: Sick of looks like fed up with; sick alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: in British English sick is also a noun for vomit.

clue.text: Tend to hold against hack

indicators.note: the tend word holds against inside it

blocks.note: to care for someone is to tend them

explanation.surface: A tendency to side against journalists.
explanation.walkthrough: Hack looks like a journalist, but it is the verb to chop.
explanation.definitionFit: Near synonym: both verbs mean cutting into something with a blade, one neatly, one roughly.

clue.text: Fresh as an arse?

blocks.note: an arse is made of two cheeks

explanation.surface: Something as lively and new as a backside.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is a joke: an arse is cheek-y because it consists of cheeks.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh has an informal sense of impertinent; the second sense jokes that a backside is all cheeks.

clue.text: Old family member canes erring politician (not bottom)

indicators.note: the canes go astray, so their letters move
drops the last letter of the politician

explanation.surface: An old relative wields the cane on a misbehaving MP.
explanation.walkthrough: Canes looks like a verb of punishment; it is only letters to mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a forebear, someone in your line who lived generations back.
